definitions.explanation: Operating something by hand rather than automatically. Used for machines, devices, and systems that require direct human control, as opposed to automatic or automated operation.

examples.japanese: この{機械|きかい}は{手動|しゅどう}で{操作|そうさ}する。
{自動|じどう}モードがうまくいかない{場合|ばあい}は{手動|しゅどう}に{切|き}り{替|か}えてください。
examples.english: If automatic mode doesn't work, please switch to manual.

examples.japanese: {手動|しゅどう}での{入力|にゅうりょく}は{時間|じかん}がかかるが、{正確|せいかく}さでは{自動|じどう}に{勝|まさ}ることもある。
examples.english: Manual input takes time, but it can surpass automatic input in accuracy.

notes:
USAGE:
Functions as a noun and as a no-adjective to modify other nouns. Almost always contrasted with {自動|じどう} (automatic). Commonly used in technical, mechanical, and computing contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手動|しゅどう}{操作|そうさ}: manual operation
- {手動|しゅどう}に{切|き}り{替|か}える: to switch to manual
- {手動|しゅどう}{入力|にゅうりょく}: manual input/entry
- {手動|しゅどう}モード: manual mode

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自動|じどう}: automatic (antonym)
- {手作業|てさぎょう}: manual work, handwork (emphasizes physical labor)
